grh_a55c6a1469c99513327f.title: Bull Story
paragraphs: Texas rancher Ned and wealthy neighbor Leland carry on an old family feud that flares after Ned's prize Aberdeen Angus bull, Boo, wins a third straight fair ribbon. Leland covets Boo and needles Ned about money, land and Ned's son Bobby, who has recently quit football. During a violent storm Boo escapes, and Bobby follows him to an abandoned oil rig where collapsing steel traps and badly injures his leg. Ned needs Leland's winch truck to free him, but Leland initially tries to exploit the emergency by demanding Boo in exchange. Ned refuses because Boo now belongs to Bobby. Bobby's courage eventually shames Leland into helping with the rescue, and Bobby prevents Ned from turning the feud into murder. By the end, Ned's family decides not to sell the ranch, Boo remains Bobby's, and they prepare to face Leland again at the next fair.

grh_a5b4890e7bfc3e0228e5.title: The No Good
paragraphs: The school board dismisses poor, troublesome teenager Lem Tolan as a no-good boy unworthy of a scholarship, but Dr. Christian sees intelligence and possibility beneath his record of mischief. When the family workhorse Noble breaks a leg and Lem becomes physically ill from fear that his father will shoot it, Dr. Christian realizes that the boy needs responsibility more than punishment. He arranges treatment for Noble and makes Lem responsible for the horse's difficult recovery, with the boy working off the expense at the doctor's office. Months of patient care transform Lem's behavior and prove his character, and the same scholarship committee finally agrees that he deserves the educational chance Dr. Christian wanted for him from the start.

grh_a5cde611b2bddbf5d6be.title: Suggestions For Divorce
paragraphs: Joan Lyman's jealousy has driven her marriage to Steve toward divorce, especially after she becomes convinced he is involved with his secretary. Dr. Christian tells Joan that her suspicion helped create the very estrangement she feared and urges her to become again the woman Steve originally loved. When Joan and Christian unexpectedly meet Steve and the other woman at a restaurant, Christian forces the situation into the open instead of letting either side retreat. A discussion of divorce arrangements turns into a revealing quarrel, and Steve's companion decides she wants no part of the marriage or its baggage. With the outside relationship ended, Joan and Steve finally admit their own faults and reconcile before the divorce is completed.

grh_a53ccc34c21a124b4f65.title: The Glamour Girl
paragraphs: Faith Denton fears that her husband Don is being drawn back to glamorous Brenda Baldwin, so Dr. Christian advises the quiet wife to remind Don that she can be exciting too. Faith transforms herself into Rivers End's new glamour girl, only to discover that Don dislikes the endless parties and begins seeking peace and sympathy from Brenda instead. The experiment reaches its breaking point when a snow-damaged roof begins collapsing during a children's program: Brenda panics, while Faith calmly plays a march and helps lead the children to safety before being injured herself. Seeing his wife's courage jolts Don back to what he nearly threw away, and Faith's recovery restores their marriage on firmer ground.

grh_a518905c1a1841b25077.title: The Last Awakening
paragraphs: After a flood, scores of Rivers End residents suddenly fall into a deep, unnatural sleep, filling the hospital and provoking an airtight quarantine around the town. Dr. Christian notices that the victims are medically normal and traces the mystery to the waterworks, where Mayor Andrews personally tried to replenish a depleted chlorine supply. In the rush, cylinders of chloral were mistaken for chlorine; mixed into the water, the chemical formed chloral hydrate, effectively dosing the town with a powerful sleeping drug. Once the accidental contamination is identified, the terrifying epidemic is revealed to be a massive but temporary poisoning rather than a new disease.

grh_a57435558c56b1a73423.title: The Devil That Calls In The Night
paragraphs: Young widow Margie is living in the old Blackwood house with her baby, little Jeffrey, and the domineering Lucinda when she begins hearing the voice of her dead husband Jeff calling to her at night. The unseen voice, mysterious objects and other frightening incidents steadily convince Margie that she is losing her mind. Dr. Christian is called after elderly servant Amos runs from the house in terror and collapses dead, insisting that a devil is loose inside. Remembering the houses old speaking-tube system, the doctor suspects a very human explanation. He has Tom imitate Jeffs voice through the tube, and Lucinda reacts in a way that exposes the scheme. She admits that she has been whispering to Margie and planting reminders of Jeff, first to frighten her into staying and later in hopes of driving her insane or to suicide so Lucinda could become guardian of the child. Dr. Christian removes Margie and the baby from the house, supports her future with Tom, and warns Lucinda that he will reveal the entire story, including the circumstances surrounding Amos death, if she tries to interfere.
GRH catalogs [[show|dr-christian|Dr. Christian]]'s "The Devil That Calls In The Night" for May 15, 1946, as episode 390.
The surviving audio runs about 24 minutes.
